# Seth Bryant

[Flood risk, from observation to impact.]{.hero-statement}

I am a **Postdoctoral Research Associate at the University of Wisconsin–Madison**, working in Beth Tellman's lab.
I combine hydraulic engineering, Earth observation, and research software to understand flooding and improve flood-risk assessment.

My work asks how terrain, infrastructure, spatial resolution, and uncertainty shape estimates of flood hazard and its consequences.

## Research focus

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-item}
[01 / HAZARD]{.section-number}

### Flood mapping across scales

Terrain-conditioned downscaling and physics-guided super-resolution connect regional flood grids with the detail needed to examine local inundation.

[Downscaling research →](projects.qmd#flood-super-resolution)
:::

::: {.research-item}
[02 / OBSERVATION]{.section-number}

### Learning from observed floods

Multisensor satellite mapping, deep learning, and scalable geospatial processing support flood-event reconstruction and model evaluation.

[Satellite-based projects →](projects.qmd#us-floods)
:::

::: {.research-item}
[03 / IMPACT]{.section-number}

### Risk and infrastructure

I examine how spatial aggregation, nonlinear damage relationships, and infrastructure disruption affect estimates of flood losses and access to essential services.

[Related publications →](publications.qmd)
:::
:::

::: {.background-grid}
::: {}
## Background

I earned a **Doctor of Engineering at the University of Potsdam in 2024**, conducting research with GFZ on aggregation and disaggregation in flood-risk models.
I previously completed an **MSc in Water Resources Engineering at the University of Alberta** and a **BSc in Civil Engineering at Montana State University**.

My research builds on professional experience in river and hydraulic engineering, flood-risk assessment, and public-sector implementation.
Alongside academia, I lead [CEFlood](https://ceflood.com), connecting research methods with engineering practice.
:::
